verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν σαββάτῳ διαπορεύεσθαι αὐτὸν διὰ σπορίμων καὶ ἔτιλλον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤσθιον τοὺς στάχυας ψώχοντες ταῖς χερσίν
verses.transliteration: Egeneto de en sabbatō diaporeuesthai auton dia sporimōn kai etillon hoi mathētai autou kai ēsthion tous stachyas psōchontes tais chersin
verses.literal: One Sabbath - Jesus was passing through the grainfields and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain rub them in their hands and eat them

verses.original: τινὲς δὲ τῶν Φαρισαίων εἶπαν Τί ποιεῖτε ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν
verses.transliteration: tines de tōn Pharisaiōn eipan Ti poieite ho ouk exestin tois sabbasin
verses.literal: But some of the Pharisees asked Why are you doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath

verses.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐδὲ τοῦτο ἀνέγνωτε ὃ ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὁπότε ἐπείνασεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ὄντες
verses.transliteration: Kai apokritheis pros autous eipen ho Iēsous Oude touto anegnōte ho epoiēsen Dauid hopote epeinasen autos kai hoi met’ autou ontes
verses.literal: Jesus replied . . . . . . . . . Have you not read what David did when he and his companions . . . . . . . . . were hungry

verses.original: ὡς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως λαβὼν ἔφαγεν καὶ ἔδωκεν τοῖς μετ’ αὐτοῦ οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν φαγεῖν εἰ μὴ μόνους τοὺς ἱερεῖς
verses.transliteration: hōs eisēlthen eis ton oikon tou Theou kai tous artous tēs protheseōs labōn ephagen kai edōken tois met’ autou hous ouk exestin phagein ei mē monous tous hiereis
verses.literal: He entered . . . the house of God took the consecrated bread . . . . . . and gave it to his companions . . . . . . and ate what is lawful only for . . . . . . the priests to eat

verses.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Κύριός ἐστιν τοῦ σαββάτου ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου
verses.transliteration: kai elegen autois Kyrios estin tou sabbatou ho Huios tou anthrōpou
verses.literal: Then Jesus declared The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ἑτέρῳ σαββάτῳ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν καὶ διδάσκειν καὶ ἦν ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖ καὶ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ ἡ δεξιὰ ἦν ξηρά
verses.transliteration: Egeneto de en heterō sabbatō eiselthein auton eis tēn synagōgēn kai didaskein kai ēn anthrōpos ekei kai hē cheir autou hē dexia ēn xēra
verses.literal: On another Sabbath - Jesus entered . . . the synagogue and was teaching and a man was there whose right hand was withered

verses.original: παρετηροῦντο δὲ αὐτὸν οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι εἰ ἐν τῷ σαββάτῳ θεραπεύει ἵνα εὕρωσιν κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: paretērounto de auton hoi grammateis kai hoi Pharisaioi ei en tō sabbatō therapeuei hina heurōsin katēgorein autou
verses.literal: Looking for a reason to accuse Jesus the scribes and Pharisees were watching Him closely . . . to see if He would heal on the Sabbath

verses.original: Αὐτὸς δὲ ᾔδει τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν εἶπεν δὲ τῷ ἀνδρὶ τῷ ξηρὰν ἔχοντι τὴν χεῖρα Ἔγειρε καὶ στῆθι εἰς τὸ μέσον καὶ ἀναστὰς ἔστη
verses.transliteration: Autos de ēdei tous dialogismous autōn eipen de tō andri tō xēran echonti tēn cheira Egeire kai stēthi eis to meson kai anastas estē
verses.literal: But Jesus knew their thoughts and said to the man with the withered hand Get up and stand among us So he got up and stood there

verses.original: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς αὐτούς Ἐπερωτῶ ὑμᾶς εἰ ἔξεστιν τῷ σαββάτῳ ἀγαθοποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι ψυχὴν σῶσαι ἢ ἀπολέσαι
verses.transliteration: eipen de ho Iēsous pros autous Eperōtō hymas ei exestin tō sabbatō agathopoiēsai ē kakopoiēsai psychēn sōsai ē apolesai
verses.literal: Then Jesus said to them I ask you which is lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil to save life or to destroy it

verses.original: Καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντας αὐτοὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρά σου ὁ δὲ ἐποίησεν καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai periblepsamenos pantas autous eipen autō Ekteinon tēn cheira sou ho de epoiēsen kai apekatestathē hē cheir autou
verses.literal: And after looking around at all of them He said to the man Stretch out your hand - He did so and it was restored

verses.original: αὐτοὶ δὲ ἐπλήσθησαν ἀνοίας καὶ διελάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους τί ἂν ποιήσαιεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ
verses.transliteration: autoi de eplēsthēsan anoias kai dielaloun pros allēlous ti an poiēsaien tō Iēsou
verses.literal: But the scribes and Pharisees were filled with rage and began to discuss with one another what . . . they might do to Jesus

verses.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ἐξελθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι καὶ ἦν διανυκτερεύων ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: Egeneto de en tais hēmerais tautais exelthein auton eis to oros proseuxasthai kai ēn dianyktereuōn en tē proseuchē tou Theou
verses.literal: In those days Jesus went out to the mountain to pray and He spent the night in prayer to God

verses.original: καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡμέρα προσεφώνησεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκλεξάμενος ἀπ’ αὐτῶν δώδεκα οὓς καὶ ἀποστόλους ὠνόμασεν
verses.transliteration: kai hote egeneto hēmera prosephōnēsen tous mathētas autou kai eklexamenos ap’ autōn dōdeka hous kai apostolous ōnomasen
verses.literal: When daylight came He called His disciples to Him and chose twelve of them whom He also designated as apostles

verses.original: Σίμωνα ὃν καὶ ὠνόμασεν Πέτρον καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον
verses.transliteration: Simōna hon kai ōnomasen Petron kai Andrean ton adelphon autou kai Iakōbon kai Iōannēn kai Philippon kai Bartholomaion
verses.literal: Simon whom He named Peter and his brother Andrew James and John Philip and Bartholomew

verses.original: καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν καὶ Ἰάκωβον Ἁλφαίου καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν καλούμενον Ζηλωτὴν
verses.transliteration: kai Maththaion kai Thōman kai Iakōbon Halphaiou kai Simōna ton kaloumenon Zēlōtēn
verses.literal: Matthew and Thomas James son of Alphaeus and Simon called the Zealot

verses.original: καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰσκαριὼθ ὃς ἐγένετο προδότης
verses.transliteration: kai Ioudan Iakōbou kai Ioudan Iskariōth hos egeneto prodotēs
verses.literal: Judas son of James and Judas Iscariot who became a traitor

verses.original: Καὶ καταβὰς μετ’ αὐτῶν ἔστη ἐπὶ τόπου πεδινοῦ καὶ ὄχλος πολὺς μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ πλῆθος πολὺ τοῦ λαοῦ ἀπὸ πάσης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ τῆς παραλίου Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος
verses.transliteration: Kai katabas met’ autōn estē epi topou pedinou kai ochlos polys mathētōn autou kai plēthos poly tou laou apo pasēs tēs Ioudaias kai Ierousalēm kai tēs paraliou Tyrou kai Sidōnos
verses.literal: Then Jesus came down with them and stood on a level place A large crowd of His disciples was there along with a great number of people from all over Judea Jerusalem and the seacoast of Tyre and Sidon

verses.original: οἳ ἦλθον ἀκοῦσαι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰαθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν νόσων αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ ἐνοχλούμενοι ἀπὸ πνευμάτων ἀκαθάρτων ἐθεραπεύοντο
verses.transliteration: hoi ēlthon akousai autou kai iathēnai apo tōn nosōn autōn kai hoi enochloumenoi apo pneumatōn akathartōn etherapeuonto
verses.literal: They had come to hear Him and to be healed of their diseases and those troubled by unclean spirits were healed

verses.original: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐζήτουν ἅπτεσθαι αὐτοῦ ὅτι δύναμις παρ’ αὐτοῦ ἐξήρχετο καὶ ἰᾶτο πάντας
verses.transliteration: kai pas ho ochlos ezētoun haptesthai autou hoti dynamis par’ autou exērcheto kai iato pantas
verses.literal: The entire crowd was trying to touch Him because power was coming from Him and healing them all

verses.original: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔλεγεν Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοί Ὅτι ὑμετέρα ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ
verses.transliteration: Kai autos eparas tous ophthalmous autou eis tous mathētas autou elegen Makarioi hoi ptōchoi Hoti hymetera estin hē basileia tou Theou
verses.literal: Looking up . . . . . . . . . at His disciples Jesus said Blessed are you who are poor for yours is the kingdom of God

verses.original: Μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες νῦν Ὅτι χορτασθήσεσθε Μακάριοι οἱ κλαίοντες νῦν Ὅτι γελάσετε
verses.transliteration: Makarioi hoi peinōntes nyn Hoti chortasthēsesthe Makarioi hoi klaiontes nyn Hoti gelasete
verses.literal: Blessed are you who hunger now for you will be filled Blessed are you who weep now for you will laugh

verses.original: Μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν μισήσωσιν ὑμᾶς οἱ ἄνθρωποι καὶ ὅταν ἀφορίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ ὀνειδίσωσιν καὶ ἐκβάλωσιν τὸ ὄνομα ὑμῶν ὡς πονηρὸν ἕνεκα τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου
verses.transliteration: Makarioi este hotan misēsōsin hymas hoi anthrōpoi kai hotan aphorisōsin hymas kai oneidisōsin kai ekbalōsin to onoma hymōn hōs ponēron heneka tou Huiou tou anthrōpou
verses.literal: Blessed are you when people hate you and when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man

verses.original: χάρητε ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ σκιρτήσατε ἰδοὺ γὰρ ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ γὰρ ἐποίουν τοῖς προφήταις οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: charēte en ekeinē tē hēmera kai skirtēsate idou gar ho misthos hymōn polys en tō ouranō kata ta auta gar epoioun tois prophētais hoi pateres autōn
verses.literal: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy because . . . great is your reward in heaven For their fathers treated the prophets in the same way

verses.original: Πλὴν οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς πλουσίοις Ὅτι ἀπέχετε τὴν παράκλησιν ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: Plēn ouai hymin tois plousiois Hoti apechete tēn paraklēsin hymōn
verses.literal: But woe to you who are rich for you have already received your comfort

verses.original: Οὐαὶ ὑμῖν οἱ ἐμπεπλησμένοι νῦν Ὅτι πεινάσετε Οὐαί οἱ γελῶντες νῦν Ὅτι πενθήσετε καὶ κλαύσετε
verses.transliteration: Ouai hymin hoi empeplēsmenoi nyn Hoti peinasete Ouai hoi gelōntes nyn Hoti penthēsete kai klausete
verses.literal: Woe to you who are well fed now for you will hunger Woe to you who laugh now for you will mourn and weep

verses.original: Οὐαὶ ὅταν καλῶς ὑμᾶς εἴπωσιν πάντες οἱ ἄνθρωποι Κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ γὰρ ἐποίουν τοῖς ψευδοπροφήταις οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: Ouai hotan kalōs hymas eipōsin pantes hoi anthrōpoi Kata ta auta gar epoioun tois pseudoprophētais hoi pateres autōn
verses.literal: Woe to you when all men speak well of you for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way

verses.original: Ἀλλὰ ὑμῖν λέγω τοῖς ἀκούουσιν Ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καλῶς ποιεῖτε τοῖς μισοῦσιν ὑμᾶς
verses.transliteration: Alla hymin legō tois akouousin Agapate tous echthrous hymōn kalōs poieite tois misousin hymas
verses.literal: But to those of you who will listen I say Love your enemies do good to those who hate you

verses.original: εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς καταρωμένους ὑμᾶς προσεύχεσθε περὶ τῶν ἐπηρεαζόντων ὑμᾶς
verses.transliteration: eulogeite tous katarōmenous hymas proseuchesthe peri tōn epēreazontōn hymas
verses.literal: bless those who curse you pray for those who mistreat you

verses.original: τῷ τύπτοντί σε ἐπὶ τὴν σιαγόνα πάρεχε καὶ τὴν ἄλλην καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντός σου τὸ ἱμάτιον καὶ τὸν χιτῶνα μὴ κωλύσῃς
verses.transliteration: tō typtonti se epi tēn siagona pareche kai tēn allēn kai apo tou airontos sou to himation kai ton chitōna mē kōlysēs
verses.literal: If someone strikes you on one cheek turn to him the other also And if someone takes your cloak do not withhold your tunic as well

verses.original: παντὶ αἰτοῦντί σε δίδου καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντος τὰ σὰ μὴ ἀπαίτει
verses.transliteration: panti aitounti se didou kai apo tou airontos ta sa mē apaitei
verses.literal: Give to everyone who asks you and if anyone takes what is yours do not demand it back

verses.original: καὶ καθὼς θέλετε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ἄνθρωποι ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς ὁμοίως
verses.transliteration: kai kathōs thelete hina poiōsin hymin hoi anthrōpoi poieite autois homoiōs
verses.literal: Do to others as you would have - them do to you

verses.original: Καὶ εἰ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν καὶ γὰρ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας αὐτοὺς ἀγαπῶσιν
verses.transliteration: Kai ei agapate tous agapōntas hymas poia hymin charis estin kai gar hoi hamartōloi tous agapōntas autous agapōsin
verses.literal: If you love those who love you what credit is that to you Even sinners love those who love them

verses.original: καὶ γὰρ ἐὰν ἀγαθοποιῆτε τοὺς ἀγαθοποιοῦντας ὑμᾶς ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν
verses.transliteration: kai gar ean agathopoiēte tous agathopoiountas hymas poia hymin charis estin kai hoi hamartōloi to auto poiousin
verses.literal: If you do good to those who do good to you what credit is that to you Even sinners do the same

verses.original: καὶ ἐὰν δανίσητε παρ’ ὧν ἐλπίζετε λαβεῖν ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἁμαρτωλοῖς δανίζουσιν ἵνα ἀπολάβωσιν τὰ ἴσα
verses.transliteration: kai ean danisēte par’ hōn elpizete labein poia hymin charis estin kai hamartōloi hamartōlois danizousin hina apolabōsin ta isa
verses.literal: And if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment what credit is that to you Even sinners lend to sinners expecting to be repaid in full

verses.original: Πλὴν ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καὶ ἀγαθοποιεῖτε καὶ δανίζετε μηδὲν ἀπελπίζοντες καὶ ἔσται ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολύς καὶ ἔσεσθε υἱοὶ Ὑψίστου ὅτι αὐτὸς χρηστός ἐστιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀχαρίστους καὶ πονηρούς
verses.transliteration: Plēn agapate tous echthrous hymōn kai agathopoieite kai danizete mēden apelpizontes kai estai ho misthos hymōn polys kai esesthe huioi Hypsistou hoti autos chrēstos estin epi tous acharistous kai ponērous
verses.literal: But love your enemies do good to them and lend to them expecting nothing in return . . . Then your reward will be great and you will be sons of the Most High for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked

verses.original: Γίνεσθε οἰκτίρμονες καθὼς καὶ ὁ Πατὴρ ὑμῶν οἰκτίρμων ἐστίν
verses.transliteration: Ginesthe oiktirmones kathōs kai ho Patēr hymōn oiktirmōn estin
verses.literal: Be merciful just as your Father is merciful

verses.original: Καὶ μὴ κρίνετε καὶ οὐ μὴ κριθῆτε καὶ μὴ καταδικάζετε καὶ οὐ μὴ καταδικασθῆτε ἀπολύετε καὶ ἀπολυθήσεσθε
verses.transliteration: Kai mē krinete kai ou mē krithēte kai mē katadikazete kai ou mē katadikasthēte apolyete kai apolythēsesthe
verses.literal: Do not judge and you will not be judged Do not condemn and you will not be condemned Forgive and you will be forgiven

verses.original: δίδοτε καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν μέτρον καλὸν πεπιεσμένον σεσαλευμένον ὑπερεκχυννόμενον δώσουσιν εἰς τὸν κόλπον ὑμῶν ᾧ γὰρ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε ἀντιμετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: didote kai dothēsetai hymin metron kalon pepiesmenon sesaleumenon hyperekchynnomenon dōsousin eis ton kolpon hymōn hō gar metrō metreite antimetrēthēsetai hymin
verses.literal: Give and it will be given to you A good measure pressed down shaken together and running over will be poured into your lap For with the measure you use it will be measured back to you

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ καὶ παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς Μήτι δύναται τυφλὸς τυφλὸν ὁδηγεῖν οὐχὶ ἀμφότεροι εἰς βόθυνον ἐμπεσοῦνται
verses.transliteration: Eipen de kai parabolēn autois Mēti dynatai typhlos typhlon hodēgein ouchi amphoteroi eis bothynon empesountai
verses.literal: Jesus also told . . . them a parable Can a blind man lead a blind man Will they not both fall into a pit

verses.original: οὐκ ἔστιν μαθητὴς ὑπὲρ τὸν διδάσκαλον κατηρτισμένος δὲ πᾶς ἔσται ὡς ὁ διδάσκαλος αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: ouk estin mathētēs hyper ton didaskalon katērtismenos de pas estai hōs ho didaskalos autou
verses.literal: A disciple is not above his teacher but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher

verses.original: Τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου τὴν δὲ δοκὸν τὴν ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ ὀφθαλμῷ οὐ κατανοεῖς
verses.transliteration: Ti de blepeis to karphos to en tō ophthalmō tou adelphou sou tēn de dokon tēn en tō idiō ophthalmō ou katanoeis
verses.literal: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye but fail to notice the beam in your own eye

verses.original: πῶς δύνασαι λέγειν τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου Ἀδελφέ ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σου αὐτὸς τὴν ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ δοκὸν οὐ βλέπων ὑποκριτά ἔκβαλε πρῶτον τὴν δοκὸν ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου ἐκβαλεῖν
verses.transliteration: pōs dynasai legein tō adelphō sou Adelphe aphes ekbalō to karphos to en tō ophthalmō sou autos tēn en tō ophthalmō sou dokon ou blepōn hypokrita ekbale prōton tēn dokon ek tou ophthalmou sou kai tote diablepseis to karphos to en tō ophthalmō tou adelphou sou ekbalein
verses.literal: How can you say - Brother let me take the speck out of your eye while you yourself fail to see the beam in your own eye You hypocrite First take the beam out of your own eye and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from - your brother’s eye

verses.original: Οὐ γάρ ἐστιν δένδρον καλὸν ποιοῦν καρπὸν σαπρόν οὐδὲ πάλιν δένδρον σαπρὸν ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλόν
verses.transliteration: Ou gar estin dendron kalon poioun karpon sapron oude palin dendron sapron poioun karpon kalon
verses.literal: No good tree bears bad fruit nor does a bad tree bear good fruit

verses.original: ἕκαστον γὰρ δένδρον ἐκ τοῦ ἰδίου καρποῦ γινώσκεται οὐ γὰρ ἐξ ἀκανθῶν συλλέγουσιν σῦκα οὐδὲ ἐκ βάτου σταφυλὴν τρυγῶσιν
verses.transliteration: hekaston gar dendron ek tou idiou karpou ginōsketai ou gar ex akanthōn syllegousin syka oude ek batou staphylēn trygōsin
verses.literal: For each tree is known by its own fruit Indeed figs are not gathered from thornbushes nor grapes from brambles

verses.original: ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ τῆς καρδίας αὐτοῦ προφέρει τὸ ἀγαθόν καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ προφέρει τὸ πονηρόν ἐκ γὰρ περισσεύματος καρδίας λαλεῖ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: ho agathos anthrōpos ek tou agathou thēsaurou tēs kardias autou propherei to agathon kai ho ponēros ek tou ponērou propherei to ponēron ek gar perisseumatos kardias lalei to stoma autou
verses.literal: The good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart and the evil man brings evil things out of the evil treasure of his heart For out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks

verses.original: Τί δέ με καλεῖτε Κύριε κύριε καὶ οὐ ποιεῖτε ἃ λέγω
verses.transliteration: Ti de me kaleite Kyrie kyrie kai ou poieite ha legō
verses.literal: Why do you call Me Lord Lord but do not do what I say

verses.original: Πᾶς ὁ ἐρχόμενος πρός με καὶ ἀκούων μου τῶν λόγων καὶ ποιῶν αὐτούς ὑποδείξω ὑμῖν τίνι ἐστὶν ὅμοιος
verses.transliteration: Pas ho erchomenos pros me kai akouōn mou tōn logōn kai poiōn autous hypodeixō hymin tini estin homoios
verses.literal: I will show you what he is like who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them

verses.original: ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομοῦντι οἰκίαν ὃς ἔσκαψεν καὶ ἐβάθυνεν καὶ ἔθηκεν θεμέλιον ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν πλημμύρης δὲ γενομένης προσέρηξεν ὁ ποταμὸς τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν σαλεῦσαι αὐτὴν διὰ τὸ καλῶς οἰκοδομῆσθαι αὐτήν
verses.transliteration: homoios estin anthrōpō oikodomounti oikian hos eskapsen kai ebathynen kai ethēken themelion epi tēn petran plēmmyrēs de genomenēs proserēxen ho potamos tē oikia ekeinē kai ouk ischysen saleusai autēn dia to kalōs oikodomēsthai autēn
verses.literal: He is like a man building a house who dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock When the flood came the torrent crashed against that house but could not shake it because it was well built . . .

verses.original: ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας καὶ μὴ ποιήσας ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομήσαντι οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν χωρὶς θεμελίου ᾗ προσέρηξεν ὁ ποταμός καὶ εὐθὺς συνέπεσεν καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ ῥῆγμα τῆς οἰκίας ἐκείνης μέγα
verses.transliteration: ho de akousas kai mē poiēsas homoios estin anthrōpō oikodomēsanti oikian epi tēn gēn chōris themeliou hē proserēxen ho potamos kai euthys synepesen kai egeneto to rhēgma tēs oikias ekeinēs mega
verses.literal: But the one who hears My words and does not act on them is like a man who built his house on ground without a foundation The torrent crashed against that house and immediately it fell and great was its destruction
